purpose: Define the vertical bar operator as the primitive admissible participation separator used inside distinction-generating expressions.

definition.name: Admissible Participation Separator
definition.reading: A | B denotes an oriented participation interface between A and B inside a distinction-generating expression.
definition.primitive_role: The operator does not by itself assert equality, division, opposition, or object-boundary separation. It establishes the structured interface through which distinction can be evaluated.

valid_operands: domain-specific projections explicitly typed as admissible operands
invalid_operands: pure scalar quantities without participation type
semantic placeholders with no admissibility trace
operand_rules.operand_requirement: Each operand must either carry an admissibility trace or be explicitly marked as awaiting admissibility qualification.

orientation_rules.orientation_statement: A | B is not generally equivalent to B | A.
orientation_rules.candidate_relation: D(A | B) may differ from D(B | A) because the participation interface carries orientation.
orientation_rules.allowed_equivalence: A | B may be equivalent to B | A only under an explicitly proven admissible reversal condition.
orientation_rules.forbidden_assumption: Do not assume symmetry of | by default.

closure_rules.local_closure: A bar expression is locally closed when both operands are admissibly typed and the interface relation is legally evaluable under D.
closure_rules.grouped_closure: Grouped bar expressions require a separate group-closure rule and are not automatically reducible to binary closure.
closure_rules.admissibility_gate: D(A | B) > epsilon_a is the minimal positive admissibility gate for distinction participation.
nonclosure_conditions: orientation reversal is assumed without proof
bar is treated as syntactic punctuation only
bar is treated as ordinary division or set separation
projection-domain meaning is imported without typed bridge

formal_candidate.reversal_condition_placeholder: Rev_|(A,B) := condition under which A|B iff_R B|A

relationship_to_D.statement: | becomes mathematically active when placed inside D(*|*) or another explicitly registered distinction-evaluating context.
relationship_to_D.warning: A|B alone is a participation expression, not yet a realized distinction unless evaluated by D or a lawful successor context.

relationship_to_Org_a.statement: Org_a may organize collections of admissible bar expressions only after the bar expressions satisfy local admissible participation closure.
relationship_to_Org_a.future_dependency: Org_a axioms may cheat Adm_|(A,B) as a prerequisite.

relationship_to_Sigma_D.statement: Sigma_D equivalence cannot be defined by operand identity alone; it must preserve admissible bar participation structure and orientation behavior.

Update vertical_bar_operator with primitive operator definition candidate
Move vertical_bar_operator from GAP_OPEN to GAP_DEFINITION_CANDIDATE
registry_updates_required.condition: Only after registry schema validation passes.

textbook_patch_required.insert_title: Vertical Bar Operator: Admissible Participation Separator
must_state: The vertical bar is not ordinary division.
The vertical bar is not mere notation.
A|B is order-sensitive unless reversal is proven.
D(A|B) > epsilon_a is the minimal admissible distinction gate.
Grouped bar expressions require a later group-closure pass.

validation_requirements: All revised registries must pass schema validation.
No downstream debt object may be marked closed by this patch alone.
forbidden_claims: A|B alone is a completed truth object

recommended_next_patch.goal: Define grouped bar participation rules for expressions such as A|B|C, (A|B)|C, A|(B|C), and triadic closures like Law|Operator|Truth.
